messages:
Maya: :warning: Seeing a big throughput drop (~35%) in us-west-2 inference pool 'pool-redwood-4' starting 09:04 UTC. Multiple worker restarts and GPU OOMs correlated with KV cache eviction rate spike. Hoping to triage quickly.
Jun: Logs show a bunch of `OOM` from worker-42/worker-47 and rapid kv_cache evict churn. attaching a small log excerpt:
```
[09:04:12] worker-42 ERROR: Alloc failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[09:04:12] runtime kernel_selector: fallback to cuda_fallback due to slab_fragmentation=0.82
[09:04:13] kv_cache: evicted 3 segments, total_evictions=1245
```
Sylvia: :eyes: Kernel selector is switching to fallback kernels when fragmentation > 0.8 — that's expensive and increases peak allocations. Also see many tiny batches from tenant-11 (small-chat bot) which increases KV pressure.
Tim: Noisy tenant hypothesis makes sense. tenant-11 had a sudden surge of tiny inference (<16 tokens) requests at 09:02 which prevents good batching and increases KV churn.
Liz: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) raise KV eviction threshold temporarily, 2) reduce per-worker max_concurrent_requests, 3) apply batch_min_tokens to coalesce tiny requests, 4) graceful restart of the most affected workers. Which do we want first?
Maya: Let's do 3 + 4: push batch_min_tokens=8 for pool-redwood-4 and restart affected workers one-by-one. Jun, can you run the command to patch the config and kick a rolling restart? I'll coordinate with SRE.
Jun: Patching config now:
```
kubectl -n inference set configmap pool-redwood-4 --from-literal=batch_min_tokens=8
# rolling restart
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/pool-redwood-4 --selector=role=worker
```
sre-bot: ALERT: worker_restarts_high detected for pool-redwood-4 — 6 restarts in 3m window. Incident created: INC-5991
deploy-bot: Starting rolling restart of deployment/pool-redwood-4 (workers=12), concurrency=1
Jun: Post-restart kube logs show reduced OOMs on restarted pods. nvtop snapshot (09:16): most GPUs at ~60% mem, no immediate OOMs. Throughput starting to recover.
Sylvia: I pulled a quick flamegraph/profile from the canary - p95 latency was 420ms during worst window vs 190ms baseline. Root cause summary from trace: excessive reallocs from kernel fallback path + KV cache compacting under high tiny-batch workload. Pseudocode of current kernel heuristic:
```
if slab_fragmentation > 0.8 or kv_eviction_rate > 100/s:
    choose kernel: cuda_fallback
else:
    choose kernel: optimized_kv_v1
```
Sylvia: Proposed follow-ups: 1) change heuristic to prefer 'kv-compact-v2' earlier (less realloc-heavy), 2) add batching heuristic to prefer merging tiny batches for noisy tenants, 3) add per-tenant slow-path throttle to prevent KV churn.
Tim: Created follow-up INF ticket INF-2123 for heuristic + batching work and owner assignment (Sylvia + Jun).
Maya: Quick summary: mitigation applied (batch_min_tokens=8 + rolling restarts), monitoring shows throughput + p95 improving. We did not change kernel code yet, only config-level mitigations. Next steps in INF-2123: kernel-selector heuristic change, KV compaction tests, add a canary for noisy-tenant throttles.
Jun: Monitoring dashboard: 09:30 UTC throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline, kv eviction rate back down to normal. Will keep watchers on for next 2 hours.
Maya: Thanks everyone. If anything flares we escalate to oncall. Marking this thread for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
